insights.summary: FY26 revenue rose 34% to ₹1,891 Cr, EBITDA margin rose to 10.6% and PAT nearly doubled to ₹132 Cr, well ahead of both the original and the raised guidance. Management says a global shortage of memory, SSDs and processors (driven by AI data centres) has pushed new laptop prices up 40-57% in six months, sending demand to refurbished PCs. It guided ~25% revenue growth and at least 50 bps higher PAT margin for FY27, and is deliberately holding high inventory (₹743 Cr) bought before prices rise.

what_changed.text: FY27: ~25% revenue growth, PAT margin up at least 50 bps, EBITDA margin ~11.5%
Distribution tie-ups with Ingram Micro and Supertron (small so far)
EMI scheme: refurbished laptops for ₹1,000 a month through dealers
Capacity of about 150,000 units a month after adding facilities in Mumbai and the UAE

tone.label: confident
tone.quote:
We have by far exceeded both the original guidance we shared at the start of the year as well as the revised
guidance we had communicated in our Q3 earnings call

analyst_questions.answer: Inventory ₹743 Cr is a deliberate bet on rising prices; net debt fell to ~₹300 Cr from ₹466 Cr in December.
New distributors need 30-45 days of credit, the same as OEMs give; to be held at that level.
Sharjah facilities ran every day; shipments go by air.

red_flags.text: Working-capital heavy: inventory ₹743 Cr (3-4 months of sales) and receivables up; borrowings back near pre-IPO levels.
Margins depend on a component price boom that management expects to last until January 2028.
Main refurbishing base is in the UAE during the Gulf conflict.

watch_next: PAT margin above 7.5% for the year
Revenue from the new national distributors

business_snapshot.what_they_make: Refurbished laptops (~81% of revenue), desktops and other IT devices under the 'Electronics Bazaar' brand, with 1-3 year warranties
business_snapshot.customers: B2B: enterprises, institutions, distributors and dealers in 46 countries; 4,895 touch points
business_snapshot.revenue_mix: FY26: India 33%, UAE 12%, US 21%, Europe 20%, rest 14%; 727,000 units at ~₹26,000 average
business_snapshot.demand_drivers: Memory and component shortage raising new-PC prices, IDC forecasting an 11% fall in new PC shipments in 2026, cost-conscious buyers
